sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 74669: Bullock, Juliann (facilitator). 2009. Wagi Wordlist, Madang Province, 2009a. 14 pp. Subject language tagged Utarmbung [omo].
sources.note: The only SIL-archive record tagged [omo] in the complete SIL OAI dump (47,956 records. The attached file is, i.e. a Wagi [fad] wordlist; the [omo] tag looks like a metadata error. PDF download returned a bot-challenge page, not retrieved. Not a stress source.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Southern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-33. xvi+113 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Osum = G3 in the comparative list (fieldwork 1971-73). Introduction sect. 9 (p. ix): 'The transcription of the wordlist is rendered semi-phonemic; i.e. apparently non-contrastive phonetic details are omitted'; stress is not marked and the words 'stress', 'accent', 'tone', 'pitch' do not occur in the volume. Grammar notes on Osum only concern obligatory noun number suffixes (sect. 10) and prefixed verbal object pronouns (sect. 13).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Published version of the thesis; same sentence at p. 6 (pdf p. 14): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' No Osum-specific phonology.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid utar1238 'Utarmbung' (and family node sout3148 South Adelbert); Hammarström et al.
sources.note: Lists only the four wordlist/overview references above; no grammar, phonology or sketch; subclassification comment cites Daniels 2015. AES: not endangered (Ethnologue 6a*).
Stub: 1,200 speakers (2003), classified Madang > Southern Adelbert > Tomul River/Josephstaal > Osum; no phonology.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975a. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study Vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress anywhere in the chapter. Osum (G3, 577 speakers) is 'The Osum family-level Isolate' extending south from Josephstaal Patrol Station towards the Sogeram River; 'Numbers are overtly marked with nouns in it' (sect. 2.8.2.2.2.4.2). Only comparative pronoun/lexical forms given.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975b. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Village census listing for Osum G3 (Alaginam, Indavaia, Ingavaia, Osum, Woguvunt, Yigebuguar) and a source index in which Osum's only bibliographic source is 'WS' = Wurm 1971 (names/classification). Confirms no description of Osum existed by 1975.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. x+335 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 13 (pdf p. 22), on the transcription of the whole Madang survey: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Osum treated only as a family-type isolate of the Josephstaal Stock (sect. 2.22.34, p. ~104) with number marking and an extra palatal nasal; nothing on Osum stress.
